question.text: Fund X is a Cat II AIF with total committed capital of INR 500 crore. The Manager issues Drawdown 1 of 20% (for Investment A) and Drawdown 2 of 15% (for Investment B). LP Z has committed INR 50 crore. After both drawdowns, what is LP Z's called (contributed) capital?

explanation.text: The Logic: Total called fraction = 20% + 15% = 35%. LP Z's called capital = 35% x INR 50 cr = INR 17.5 crore. Drawdowns are applied pro-rata across all LPs on their committed capital; same class, same terms. The Trap: Option A is 20% only (single drawdown). Option B is 25% error. Option D is 50% error — possibly confusing with committed. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test basic drawdown arithmetic. XIX-C layers multi-drawdown schedules. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always match drawdown timing to deal funding need — calling capital earlier than necessary depresses IRR (the denominator grows). LPs actively track this in quarterly IRR letters.
